headline: Power-hungry AI boom brings inflation, a 2028 crash, then a contested automation dividend

events: Early-2027 agentic models reliably run multi-day software, accounting and claims-processing tasks; enterprise AI adoption doubles to ~25% of firms
Data-centre load growth sends wholesale power prices up 30-50% in PJM, Ireland, Netherlands and Japan; utilities file record rate cases
Electricity and services inflation pushes G20 inflation back above 4%; Fed pauses cuts and the ECB holds at 2.25%
Graduate hiring in law, finance, IT outsourcing and marketing falls by a third; Indian and Philippine BPO firms announce mass layoffs
US-China agree a limited tariff truce covering chips-for-rare-earths; trade tensions plateau
Q1 'compute glut' scare: hyperscaler capex guidance cut, AI equity index falls 38%, private-credit data-centre loans sour
Fed hikes once in late 2027 then reverses with 150bp of cuts in 2028 as US unemployment climbs to 6.4%
Second capability jump (robust long-horizon agents plus cheap humanoid pilots in warehouses) restores confidence by Q4; AI stocks recover half their losses
US election dominated by job loss and power bills; winner campaigns on an 'AI windfall tax' and federal retraining wage
Global unemployment peaks near 7.1%; Philippines, Egypt and Kenya see remittance and BPO income drop
US passes Compute and Automation Revenue Act: surcharge on large-model inference revenue funds a wage-insurance scheme; deficit still ~7% of GDP
EU launches a 'Social Climate and Transition Fund 2' with joint borrowing; France and Italy introduce shorter-week pilots
Small modular reactor orders and grid-scale battery buildout accelerate; gas turbine backlogs push some data centres to on-site gas
Pakistan and Egypt restructure debt after BPO/remittance shocks and high rates; Sri Lanka-style protests in Nairobi
Measured US productivity growth hits 3.8%, the highest since the early 1950s
Third capability jump: AI systems contribute materially to drug discovery and materials science; first AI-designed antibiotic class approved
G20 inflation falls to ~2.5% as AI deflation in services offsets energy costs; real wages for top quintile surge, median flat
Mass 'humans-first' protests in France, South Korea and the US Midwest; several regional general strikes
Iran-Gulf maritime clash briefly spikes oil to $115 before a ceasefire
Argentina and Bolivia enter debt crises; IMF launches an AI-transition facility for labour-exporting economies
Over 60% of firms use AI in production; agentic 'AI employees' outnumber human staff at several Fortune 500 firms
Global unemployment eases to ~6.2% as care, construction, energy and trades absorb workers, but youth underemployment stays high in South Asia and Africa
US debt reaches ~131% of GDP despite strong growth, as wage insurance, defence and interest costs climb
Renewables reach ~44% of global electricity; data centres consume ~5% of world power
Populist parties lead polls in five G7 countries; trust in institutions at multi-decade lows

winners: US and Chinese frontier AI labs and hyperscalers
Owners of power generation, grid equipment and nuclear/battery supply chains
Skilled trades, care workers and AI-complemented senior professionals
losers: Entry-level white-collar workers and recent graduates
BPO-dependent and remittance-reliant economies (Philippines, India's IT hubs, Egypt, Kenya)
Households and energy-intensive industries facing soaring electricity bills
bullets: AI delivered the fastest productivity growth in 75 years, but gains accrued to capital and a thin skilled elite; labour share fell ~3 points in rich economies.
Electricity, not chips, became the binding constraint: power prices drove a 2027-28 inflation bump and made energy policy central to AI policy.
A sharp 2028 AI-equity crash proved a pause, not a bust, as a second capability jump revived investment.
Rich countries improvised safety nets (wage insurance, inference levies, shorter-week pilots) funded largely by more debt; global public debt passed 100% of GDP.
Services-exporting developing countries were hit hardest, producing four sovereign debt crises and a new IMF transition facility.
Trade fragmentation crept up only modestly; the US-China contest shifted to compute, energy and talent rather than tariffs.
Politics hardened: anti-automation movements, regional strikes and populist poll leads reflect deep distrust of elites and tech firms.
AI-accelerated science began producing tangible wins in medicine and materials, the main source of optimism heading into the 2030s.
wildcard: An AI-designed novel antibiotic class was approved in 2030, roughly a decade ahead of expectations.
image_description: In a Manila call-centre tower converted into a vocational school, former agents in hi-vis vests learn to service heat pumps while screens overhead show an AI agent closing ten thousand customer tickets a minute.
